cards.explanation: The answer is the Jordan, friends! The LORD says, “…cross over the Jordan into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.” Moses, Israel's leader, has died, and the LORD tells Joshua, “Now therefore arise, you and all these people…” Arise, and cross a whole river. I'd need a minute to stretch just to get up.

The answer is False, friends, and the clue is two little words: “just as.” The LORD says, “I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread, just as I promised to Moses.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. That promise has a history, so it's no fresh batch.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, “No one shall stand against you all the days of your life.” There is no list of exceptions, and no warning about a few who might still stand. When the LORD says no one, I'd take Him at His word.

The answer is Moses, Israel's leader, friends. The LORD says, “As I was with Moses, so will I be with you…” The first verse calls Joshua Moses' assistant, so Joshua had served alongside him. And then the LORD adds, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”

The answer is be strong and courageous, friends! The LORD says, “Be strong and courageous…” He has just promised to be with Joshua, and now He gives him the command for the job. Joshua is about to lead a whole people into a new land, so I'd say that's the right thing to hear.

The answer is that he will give the people the land, friends. The LORD says, “Be strong and courageous, for you shall give these people the inheritance of the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.” The land is the LORD's promise, and Joshua is the one who will hand it over. That's a big delivery job.

The answer is all the law Moses commanded, friends. The LORD says, “Be careful to observe all the law that My servant Moses commanded you.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua, and the law he gave is what Joshua is told to keep close. Courage and care go together here.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, “Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may prosper wherever you go.” It's like walking a straight line down the middle of a road. Stay on it.

The answer is day and night, friends. The LORD says, “This Book of the Law must not depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night…” That's no once-in-a-while thing. I can barely keep a batch from burning, so I'm impressed.

The word is “do,” friends! The LORD says to meditate on it “…so that you may be careful to do everything written in it.” It isn't just to have the words in his head. It's to do what the Book says. Reading a recipe never fed anybody, and I would know.
The answer is food for the journey, friends. Joshua tells the officers to say, “Prepare your provisions…” That means food for the road. I like that plan, because nobody should cross a river hungry.

The answer is to take possession of the land, friends. Joshua's message says they will “…go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.” The crossing is about the land the LORD is giving. Three days is not much time to pack.

The answer is True, friends. Joshua says, “Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. Notice the word “may,” because Joshua is giving them permission. The mighty men of valor have a different job.

The answer is to cross over armed ahead of their brothers, friends. Joshua says, “…all your mighty men of valor must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers and help them…” Their own land is already settled, but they cross first to help. That's showing up for family.

The answer is False, friends. Joshua says the fighting men help “…until the LORD gives them rest as He has done for you, and your brothers also possess the land…” Then they may return to their own land. The job lasts until their brothers have their land too.

The answer is to do everything he commands, friends. Those who answer Joshua say, “Everything you have commanded us we will do, and everywhere you send us we will go.” They don't ask for time or say maybe. It's a full yes.

The answer is True, friends. Those who answer Joshua say, “Just as we obeyed Moses in all things, so we will obey you.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. They are saying that what they gave Moses, Joshua will get too.

The answer is that they will be put to death, friends, and it's a serious line. Those who answer Joshua say, “Anyone who rebels against your order and does not obey your words, all that you command him, will be put to death.” I think this is one of the heavy parts of the passage. They aren't joking around.
